speaker: Unknown
en: So in terms of like raw time savings and the aggregate output of this, it's pretty flat between junior engineers who are using the tech more and staff engineers who have an easier time spotting hallucinations, understanding the architecture around the changes they're making and things like that.
zh: 所以就原始的时间节省和这方面的总体产出而言，在更多使用这项技术的初级工程师与更容易发现幻觉、理解所做改动周边架构的 staff 工程师之间，差距相当平。

speaker: Unknown
en: Smaller companies lead in time savings.
zh: 小公司在时间节省上领先。

speaker: Unknown
en: Sure, the release pipelines are gonna be less complicated.
zh: 当然，发布流水线不会那么复杂。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's less overall complexity in the organization that's going to lead to more time savings for a company that already has less friction and has a little bit more agility to it than a larger company.
zh: 组织的整体复杂度更低，这让一家本就摩擦更少、灵活度略高的公司比大公司节省更多时间。

speaker: Unknown
en: What about measurement?
zh: 那么度量呢？

speaker: Unknown
en: How should we even be thinking about measuring this stuff?
zh: 我们到底应该如何思考度量这些东西？

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, it bears mentioning that measuring developer productivity and measuring developer experience was a challenge before AI, and we never completed that conversation before kind of throwing accelerant on this, right?
zh: 值得一提的是，度量开发者生产力和度量开发者体验在 AI 出现之前就是一个难题，而在给这个话题浇上助燃剂之前，我们从未完成过那场对话，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: So this is still a difficult thing, and I'd argue even more difficult to do now because it's confounded by several different aspects of AI.
zh: 所以这依然是一件困难的事，而且我可以说现在做起来更加困难，因为它被 AI 的多个不同方面所混淆。

speaker: Unknown
en: But we're all gonna have to answer this question this year.
zh: 但今年我们所有人都必须回答这个问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: Right?
zh: 对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: Spent 10 million or way more if you come to my talk later today on tokens.
zh: 花了 1000 万或更多——如果你今天晚些时候来听我关于 token 的演讲的话。

speaker: Unknown
en: Where's our 10x productivity?
zh: 我们的 10 倍生产力在哪里？

speaker: Unknown
en: When we're thinking about this stuff, it's important to bear in mind that we don't throw away what we're measuring.
zh: 在思考这些问题时，重要的是要记住，我们不能抛弃我们已经在度量的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: Our foundational developer experience and developer productivity metrics are still what matter the most.
zh: 我们的基础开发体验和开发者生产力指标仍然是最重要的。

speaker: Unknown
en: We want to understand how AI is impacting these trusted metrics that we've already been looking at.
zh: 我们想理解 AI 是如何影响这些我们已经一直在关注的可信指标的。

speaker: Unknown
en: We want to maybe look at cohorts of users.
zh: 我们或许想看看用户群组。

speaker: Unknown
en: We maybe want to take data from the API telemetry and things that come out of the tools.
zh: 我们或许想从 API 遥测数据和工具产出的数据中提取信息，

speaker: Unknown
en: and use that to understand who's using what and where, but we would only want to use those cohorts and look at them comparatively across our foundational metrics.
zh: 并用它来理解谁在使用什么、在哪里使用，但我们只想使用这些群组，并在我们的基础指标上对它们进行对比观察。

speaker: Unknown
en: What is this actually doing to quality?
zh: 这实际上对质量产生了什么影响？

speaker: Unknown
en: What is this actually doing to speed?
zh: 这实际上对速度产生了什么影响？

speaker: Unknown
en: What is this doing to impact to the organization and value generation?
zh: 这对组织和价值创造产生了什么影响？

speaker: Unknown
en: And so this is where our AI measurement framework comes from.
zh: 这就是我们的 AI 度量框架的来源。

speaker: Unknown
en: I won't spend too much time on this.
zh: 我不会在这上面花太多时间。

speaker: Unknown
en: We have a big white paper available.
zh: 我们有一份很长的白皮书可供参考。

speaker: Unknown
en: My colleague Anton, who's standing in the back of the room in the white shirt, will be able to hand out some hard copies of reports that we have after the talk that go into the way that we derive this methodology and how to use it and think about it.
zh: 我的同事 Anton——他穿着白衬衫站在房间后面——在演讲结束后会发放一些我们报告的纸质版，这些报告深入讲解了我们对这套方法的推导方式，以及如何使用和思考它。

speaker: Unknown
en: It focuses on three key dimensions of measurement, so looking at utilization,
zh: 它聚焦于三个关键的度量维度，首先是使用率，

speaker: Unknown
en: Our daily active users, weekly active users, that sort of thing.
zh: 我们的日活跃用户、周活跃用户，诸如此类。

speaker: Unknown
en: It looks at impact.
zh: 它关注影响力。

speaker: Unknown
en: So which metric should we be looking for moving the needle based on utilization?
zh: 也就是说，基于使用率，我们应该关注哪个指标在起作用？

speaker: Unknown
en: As our utilization goes up, what do we hope to see in terms of impact to the business?
zh: 随着使用率上升，我们希望在业务影响方面看到什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: And then cost.
zh: 然后是成本。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's a fair joke that we're 15 years after the last major hype cycle and we're still trying to figure out cloud costs, but this stuff is getting pretty expensive.
zh: 有个挺合理的笑话是：距离上一次大型炒作周期已经过去 15 年了，我们仍在试图搞清楚云成本，但这些东西正变得相当昂贵。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're going to have to measure it.
zh: 我们将不得不去度量它。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you can think about this as a bit of a maturity curve as well.
zh: 所以你也可以把这看作一条成熟度曲线。

speaker: Unknown
en: Most people start with utilization on the left, just figuring out what's happening in the organization with the tech, who's using it, what are they using, how often and for what use cases, and then how do we then cross-reference those to the impact metrics, the value generation, what we really want to understand to know whether these investments are actually working, which is what we really want to figure out.
zh: 大多数人从左边的使用率开始，只是弄清楚组织里这项技术正在发生什么，谁在使用，他们在用什么，使用频率如何，用于什么用例，然后我们如何把这些与影响力指标、价值创造进行交叉参照——这才是我们真正想理解的，以便知道这些投资是否真的奏效，这正是我们真正想弄清楚的。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is just an example of how we might correlate such a thing.
zh: 这只是我们可能如何关联这类东西的一个例子。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you could look at two separate cohorts of users and you could compare them across metrics like PR cycle time or PR size or pushback in review, right?
zh: 你可以看两个不同的用户群组，并在诸如 PR 周期时间、PR 大小或评审中的推回（pushback）等指标上对它们进行比较，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: So lots of the way to think about this again is just right now separate cohorts and then look at how that plays out across these foundational productivity metrics that we've learned to trust.
zh: 所以，再次强调，这里很多思考方式就是：先分出不同的群组，然后观察在我们已经学会信任的那些基础生产力指标上这会如何表现。

speaker: Unknown
en: We also need to be able to understand our platform's readiness.
zh: 我们还需要能够理解我们平台的就绪度。

speaker: Unknown
en: I like to say that in 2024, we gave everybody a coding assistant.
zh: 我喜欢这么说：在 2024 年，我们给每个人配备了编程助手。

speaker: Unknown
en: In 2025, we started building agents.
zh: 在 2025 年，我们开始构建智能体。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now we're realizing that our infrastructure wasn't ready for any of this.
zh: 现在我们意识到，我们的基础设施根本没为这些东西做好准备。

speaker: Unknown
en: A lot of the vendors that are here are selling solutions that help you with this problem.
zh: 这里很多厂商正在销售的解决方案就是帮你解决这个问题的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think if you can measure your platform's AI readiness, you're gonna have a much better handle on how efficient you're gonna be spending tokens and providing context to these agents.
zh: 我认为，如果你能度量平台的 AI 就绪度，你对如何高效地消耗 token 以及为这些智能体提供上下文就会有更好的把握。

speaker: Unknown
en: So these are things like clear and accurate, well-structured documentation, data structures with straightforward relations, manageable modular code, reliable local CI and non-flaky test suites.
zh: 这些东西包括：清晰准确、结构良好的文档，关系直截了当的数据结构，可管理的模块化代码，可靠的本地 CI 以及不飘忽（non-flaky）的测试套件。

speaker: Unknown
en: If, by the way, any of this sounds familiar to you, it's because we used to just call this good developer experience, right?
zh: 顺便说一句，如果这些听起来让你觉得熟悉，那是因为我们过去只是把这称为良好的开发者体验，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: But it turns out that what's good for humans is also good for agents, so we may finally, paradoxically, be making those investments that we should have been making over the last couple of decades.
zh: 但事实证明，对人类有益的东西对智能体也有益，所以颇具悖论意味的是，我们可能终于要做那些过去几十年我们就该做的投资了。

speaker: Unknown
en: We also want to understand the effectiveness of the way that we work with AI.
zh: 我们还想理解我们与 AI 协作方式的有效性。

speaker: Unknown
en: And this is one way of doing that.
zh: 这是做到这一点的一种方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: What you're actually seeing here is feedback, qualitative feedback coming back from agents telling us where they ran into issues with steering with the human, the context that was provided for them, the feedback cycles that they had to go through.
zh: 你在这里实际看到的是反馈，即来自智能体的定性反馈，告诉我们它们在与人类的引导（steering）配合上、在为它们提供的上下文上、在它们必须经历的反馈循环上遇到了哪些问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we're actually getting that data from the agents to try to figure out how effective our teams are at working with AI and we can break this down
zh: 所以我们实际上是从智能体那里获取这些数据，试图弄清我们的团队与 AI 协作的有效性如何，我们可以把它分解

speaker: Unknown
en: into use cases which is very important too.
zh: 到用例层面，这同样非常重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: We want to understand which use cases are giving us the most efficient token spend and again moving the needle for value creation and productivity within the business.
zh: 我们想理解哪些用例给了我们最高效的 token 消耗，并再次为业务内的价值创造和生产力起到推动作用。

speaker: Unknown
en: Finally, the fifth trend, integrating across the SDLC and PDLC.
zh: 最后，第五个趋势：贯穿 SDLC 和 PDLC 的整合。

speaker: Unknown
en: Why would we want to do this?
zh: 我们为什么要这样做？

speaker: Unknown
en: Because code generation was never the bottleneck in the first place, right?
zh: 因为代码生成从一开始就不是瓶颈，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: Even if engineers are getting like 100% accurate instant code coming from the models, which they are not, you would still only be attacking anywhere from maybe 14 to 16% of the overall value stream.
zh: 即使工程师从模型那里得到的是 100% 准确的即时代码——事实并非如此——你仍然只是在攻击整个价值流中大约 14% 到 16% 的部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we need to think beyond that, especially because right now the productivity gains that we are actually seeing are more modest than expected.
zh: 所以我们需要思考超越这个范围的东西，尤其是因为目前我们实际看到的生产力提升比预期要温和。

speaker: Unknown
en: Despite additional PR throughput increases, our median increase in the study that we did from November to 2024 to February this year only found about a median 7.7% increase in this velocity metric, a 13% average, but even our top performers were in the 70% range.
zh: 尽管 PR 吞吐量有所增加，但我们在从 2024 年 11 月到今年 2 月所做的研究中发现，这个速度指标的中位数增长只有约 7.7%，平均值为 13%，但即使是我们的表现最好者也只在 70% 的区间。

speaker: Unknown
en: Nobody hit 2x, nobody hit 5x, nobody hit 10x.
zh: 没有人达到 2 倍，没有人达到 5 倍，没有人达到 10 倍。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's because our time savings that come out of AI are still being outweighed by other non-AI factors within our organization, right?
zh: 这是因为我们从 AI 中获得的时间节省，仍然被我们组织内部其他非 AI 因素所抵消，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: We might be saving a lot of time with AI and that's great, but if we're still eclipsing those time savings because of meeting heavy days and context switching and other sources of interruption,
zh: 我们可能通过 AI 节省了大量时间，这很棒，但如果我们仍然因为会议缠身的日子、上下文切换和其他干扰源而抵消了那些时间节省，

speaker: Unknown
en: The cumulative effects of the dev environment and friction in the way that we create software around the code, then we're not attacking the bottleneck.
zh: 加上开发环境的累积影响以及我们在围绕代码创建软件的方式中的摩擦，那么我们就不是在攻击瓶颈。

speaker: Unknown
en: And as Ellie Goldratt from the theory of constraints and the goal and inspiration for the Phoenix project would tell us that an hour saved on something that isn't the bottleneck is worthless.
zh: 正如约束理论、《目标》的作者、《凤凰项目》灵感来源的 Ellie Goldratt 会告诉我们的那样：在非瓶颈环节节省的一小时是毫无价值的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we need to find the bottleneck and fix the bottleneck.
zh: 所以我们需要找到瓶颈并修复瓶颈。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's what a lot of organizations are doing.
zh: 这就是很多组织正在做的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: Morgan Stanley has been really public about their creation of the DevGen AI agent.
zh: Morgan Stanley 在他们创建的 DevGen AI 智能体方面一直非常公开。

speaker: Unknown
en: which is an agent for interpreting legacy code like Mainframe, Natural, and Cobalt, and I hate to admit, Perl, I've written a lot of Perl in my career, but it's legacy now.
zh: 这是一个用于解读遗留代码的智能体，比如 Mainframe、Natural 和 Cobalt，还有我不太愿意承认的 Perl——我职业生涯中写过很多 Perl，但它现在已经是遗留代码了。

speaker: Unknown
en: The agent actually creates PRDs to hand to engineers to get rid of that reverse engineering step, and it's saving Morgan Stanley about 300,000 hours a year right now.
zh: 该智能体实际上会创建 PRD 交给工程师，从而省去逆向工程这一步骤，它现在每年为 Morgan Stanley 节省大约 30 万小时。

speaker: Unknown
en: Zapier is one of my favorite stories in AI right now.
zh: Zapier 是我现在最喜欢的 AI 故事之一。

speaker: Unknown
en: They have a whole agent ecosystem that they're using to deal with a lot of administrative tasks and overhead, like daily stand-ups and things like that.
zh: 他们有一整套智能体生态系统，用来处理大量行政事务和开销，比如每日站会之类的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: They've reduced their stand-ups by using agent summaries and things like that in this ecosystem that they've built.
zh: 他们通过在这个生态系统中使用智能体摘要之类的东西，减少了站会。

speaker: Unknown
en: to two times a week as opposed to five times a week.
zh: 从每周五次减少到每周两次。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're successfully onboarding engineers within about a two week period which is really fast.
zh: 他们能在大约两周内成功完成工程师入职，这真的非常快。

speaker: Unknown
en: Our industry benchmark for that is over a month usually.
zh: 我们在这方面的行业基准通常是一个月以上。

speaker: Unknown
en: But my favorite part about this story is that they're seeing about a 15% additional value creation per engineer, so they are hiring more than they have in the history of their entire company because they realize the truth here, that they're getting more capacity per single engineer, they're getting a better return on investment per single engineer, and hiring more engineers will improve their competitive edge.
zh: 但这个故事里我最喜欢的部分是，他们看到每位工程师带来了大约 15% 的额外价值创造，所以他们的招聘规模超过了公司整个历史上任何时期，因为他们认识到了这里的真相：他们从单个工程师身上获得了更多产能，从单个工程师身上获得了更好的投资回报，而招聘更多工程师将提升他们的竞争优势。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is the right attitude.
zh: 这是正确的态度。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is a throughput story.
zh: 这是一个吞吐量的故事。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is an increased innovative capacity story.
zh: 这是一个创新能力提升的故事。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is not a headcount replacement story.
zh: 这不是一个替换人力的故事。

speaker: Unknown
en: FAIR, they're automating about 3,000 of their code reviews a week triggered off of a pull request.
zh: FAIR，他们每周自动化大约 3,000 次由拉取请求触发的代码审查。

speaker: Unknown
en: And they look at superficial stuff.
zh: 而且他们只看表面层次的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: They still need humans in the loop.
zh: 他们仍然需要人类参与其中。

speaker: Unknown
en: But the initial superficial review that comes from the agent is all part of the system of record.
zh: 但来自智能体的最初表面审查全都属于记录系统的一部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: It stays in the PR comments.
zh: 它会保留在 PR 评论中。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so the next engineer to actually perform the review will have an idea of what the agent's already looked at.
zh: 所以下一个真正执行审查的工程师会了解智能体已经看过哪些内容。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it can save some time.
zh: 这样就能节省一些时间。

speaker: Unknown
en: Finally, Spotify, if anybody remembers the Spotify model from DevOps, they were sort of the North Star for DevOps.
zh: 最后是 Spotify，如果还有人记得 DevOps 领域的 Spotify 模型，他们曾经是 DevOps 的指路明灯。

speaker: Unknown
en: They built an agent for SREs that will gather remediation steps from runbooks and information in context about the incident and put all that together into SRE communication channels so that when an incident occurs, the SRE has immediate context and doesn't have to go through multiple minutes of discovery to figure out how to solve the issue.
zh: 他们为 SRE 构建了一个智能体，它会从 runbook 和事件相关的上下文信息中收集修复步骤，并将所有这些汇总到 SRE 的沟通渠道中，这样当事件发生时，SRE 就能立即获得上下文，而不必花费好几分钟的排查来弄清楚如何解决问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: So if you want to dive deeper into this data, our Q2 report is coming out in just a few weeks, but the Q1 report still has a lot of tidbits from this session in it.
zh: 所以如果你想深入了解这些数据，我们的 Q2 报告将在几周内发布，但 Q1 报告中仍然包含本次分享中的很多有用信息。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if you subscribe to our newsletter or you come back to the website, by mid-ish end of July, we'll have our Q2 report.
zh: 如果你订阅了我们的简报，或者回到我们网站查看，到 7 月中旬左右，我们就会发布 Q2 报告。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if you want to see a preview of that report, that's the talk that I'm giving later this afternoon.
zh: 如果你想提前看这份报告的预览，那就是我今天下午晚些时候要做的演讲。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thanks everybody for your time, I appreciate it.
zh: 感谢大家的时间，非常感谢。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thank you.
zh: 谢谢。
